newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia wants MAS to share future landing rights.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia wants MAS to share future landing rights.

text.p: Malaysian Airline System Bhd (MAS), the national carrier, will no longer be given the priority in future to have landing rights obtained by the government, Transport Minister Ling Liong Sik said on Sunday.
MAS will have to share future landing rights with other local airlines such as Air Asia, the national Bernama news agency quoted him as saying.
"We cannot say that all the future landing rights belong to MAS and that nobody else should have them except MAS," Ling told reporters.
However, he said the existing landing rights which MAS already had would not be affected.

"We don't want to end up in a monopoly situation, but we would continue to consider MAS because we want MAS to be viable. On the other hand, we have other airlines who have spent millions buying new aircrafts, and we cannot say sorry no flight, you just sit on the ground and wait'," he said.
Ling said MAS and Air Asia were currently bidding for new landing rights to several Chinese cities which the government recently obtained.
"The government would like them to share the rights and had instructed them to discuss how they are going to share them," he said.
The landing rights approved by the Chinese authorities consist of twice weekly flights each to Shanghai and a full freight service to Shenzhen.
Malaysia can also operate a twice-weekly flight to Xiamen, in the Fukien province, once China takes up its fifth freedom right from Bangkok to Kuala Lumpur.
Malaysia has a number of other small airline companies which provide local and regional services.
